ai.description: This slender racer reaches 100 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct dark, light-edged stripe extending along the tail. It features a narrow head and large eyes, distinguishing it from similar species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Platyceps vittacaudatus* is uniquely identified by the distinct, continuous dark stripe running along the center of its tail, which is absent in other similar racers.
ai.habitat: The Striped-tailed Racer inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate altitudes in rocky, arid terrain.
ai.behavior: The Striped-tailed Racer is primarily diurnal, actively hunting for small lizards and rodents across rocky, arid landscapes during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Platyceps vittacaudatus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally between April and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Platyceps vittacaudatus* is endemic to the arid regions of Pakistan and northwestern India, primarily inhabiting the Thar Desert and surrounding semi-arid zones.
